newsitem.title: UK: P&O tumbles after report of U.S. lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: P&O tumbles after report of U.S. lawsuit.

text.p: Shares in Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc tumbled in early trading on Thursday as a report in Lloyd's List newspaper said the company faces a U.S. lawsuit over alleged unfair trading practices.
The stock was down 29-1/2p at 611 by 0830 GMT in volume of 884,292 shares.
The paper said P&O's Princess Cruises unit was being sued by the state of Florida, seeking fines of up to $15,000 for each passenger boarded at state ports over the last four years.
It said Florida attorney-general Bob Butterworth said Princess had been "pocketing" money collected as port charges that customers were led to believe was a government fee.
"It could be hugely damaging to P&O," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage.
The paper said the total size of any possible fines was not known.
The lawsuit was first reported on Wednesday, when Florida said the fees added as much as $150 to advertised ticket prices.
"By keeping portions of these add-on fees for itself, Princess was able to advertise lower cruise prices than would otherwise be possible," Butterworth said.
Princess responded with a statement saying the charges had no merit and that Florida had never detailed any violation committed by Princess.
"We believe that our advertising in the state of Florida had always communicated to consumers the full price of the cruise...," the company said.
No-one at P&O in London was immediately available for further comment.
